title: Chapter 11 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of CSS Grid: tracks, placement, gaps, alignment, and template areas!

questions.question: To turn an element into a grid container, you use:
questions.explanation: `display: grid;` or `inline-grid` creates a grid context.

questions.question: Only direct children of a grid container become grid items.
questions.explanation: Just like Flexbox, the grid only affects direct children.

questions.question: What does `grid-template-columns: 100px 1fr 2fr;` produce?
options: Three columns: first 100px, second 1 fraction of leftover space, third 2 fractions
questions.explanation: It creates three columns with the given sizes.

questions.question: The unit that distributes free space proportionally in a grid is ______.
questions.explanation: `fr` stands for fraction.

questions.question: How do you create four equal columns using `repeat()`?
questions.explanation: `repeat(4, 1fr)` is the correct syntax.

questions.question: What is the purpose of `minmax()` in grid definitions?
options: To set a minimum and maximum gap size
To define a track size that flexes between a lower and upper bound
To constrain the number of columns
To specify the minimum number of items per row
questions.explanation: `minmax(min, max)` sets a range for the track size.

questions.question: What does `grid-column: 1 / 3;` set?
options: The item starts at column line 1 and ends at column line 3 (spans columns 1 and 2)
The item occupies columns 1 to 3 (three columns)
The item is placed in column 1, row 3
questions.explanation: `1 / 3` means start at line 1, end at line 3, spanning two column tracks.

questions.question: How would you make an item span 3 columns using `span`?
options: both a and b are valid
questions.explanation: Both `grid-column: span 3;` (auto‑start) and `grid-column: 1 / span 3;` (explicit start) work.

questions.question: With `grid-template-columns: [main-start] 1fr [main-end];`, how do you position an item to fill that column?
questions.explanation: You reference the named lines.

questions.question: What does `gap: 10px 20px;` set?
questions.explanation: First value is row-gap, second is column-gap.

questions.question: Which property controls the vertical alignment of all grid items within their rows?
questions.explanation: `align-items` aligns items along the column (vertical) axis.

questions.question: What does `justify-content: center;` do in a grid?
options: Centres text inside each grid item
Centres the entire grid tracks horizontally within the container if tracks are narrower than container
questions.explanation: `justify-content` distributes grid tracks along the inline (horizontal) axis.

questions.question: Which property overrides the container's `align-items` for a single grid item?
questions.explanation: `align-self` sets vertical alignment for that specific item.

questions.question: What does `grid-template-areas: "header header" "sidebar main";` define?
options: A 2×2 grid with header spanning both columns in the first row, and sidebar and main in the second row
A 2×2 grid with header in first row, sidebar and main in second row, but header only one column
A single row with four columns
questions.explanation: Two rows: first row has 'header' spanning both columns; second row has 'sidebar' and 'main'.

questions.question: How do you assign an element to a named grid area?
questions.explanation: `grid-area` on the item matches the name defined in `grid-template-areas`.

questions.question: What does a period (.) mean in a `grid-template-areas` string?
options: A cell that must be filled
A placeholder for an empty cell
A cell that inherits from parent
questions.explanation: A period creates an empty cell.

questions.question: How can you make a grid responsive without media queries?
questions.explanation: `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(200px, 1fr))` creates as many columns as will fit.

questions.question: `grid-auto-rows` controls the size of explicitly defined rows.
questions.explanation: `grid-auto-rows` sizes implicit rows (those created automatically). Explicit rows are sized by `grid-template-rows`.

questions.question: What is the shorthand for setting both `align-items` and `justify-items`?
questions.explanation: `place-items` takes two values: first align, second justify.

questions.question: If `grid-template-areas: "a b" "c d";`, how many grid cells are defined?
questions.explanation: Two rows, each with two areas = 4 cells.

questions.question: What happens if an item is placed outside the defined explicit grid?
options: Implicit tracks are created to accommodate it
questions.explanation: Implicit tracks are added automatically; their size is controlled by `grid-auto-columns`/`grid-auto-rows`.

questions.question: Which value of `justify-content` spreads tracks with equal space around them, including half‑space at edges?
questions.explanation: `space-around` gives each track equal space on both sides, resulting in half‑gaps at ends.

questions.question: How can you change the layout order of grid items for mobile without touching HTML?
questions.explanation: By changing `grid-template-areas` at different breakpoints, you can visually reorder sections without changing HTML source.

questions.question: What does `grid-area: 2 / 1 / 4 / 3;` mean?
options: Row start 2, column start 1, row end 4, column end 3
Column start 2, row start 1, column end 4, row end 3
Row start 2, column start 4, row end 1, column end 3
questions.explanation: The `grid-area` shorthand with four values: row-start / column-start / row-end / column-end.
